covers.quote: Put a non-breaking space between the chunks of digits
Use a narrow no-break space between chunks of digits in a telephone number.

rules.quote: Use a non-breaking space between chunks of digits in a telephone number.
rules.violation_condition: chunks of digits in a telephone number separated by normal breaking spaces or punctuation instead of non-breaking spaces
when: In print contexts, a narrow no-break space (U+202F) is used instead.
rules.why: G-2: narrow no-break space for print is a variation/case of non-breaking space between digit chunks.

covers.quote: Use Australia’s national format when writing Australian telephone numbers for content that will be used within Australia.

rules.quote: For landline telephone numbers, write the 2-digit area code followed by a non-breaking space. Then write the rest of the number in 2 chunks of 4 digits.
rules.violation_condition: an Australian national landline number not formatted as 2 digits, a space, 4 digits, a space, and 4 digits (e.g. 02 5550 4321)
when: Content is intended for use within Australia.
rules.why: G-2: specific digit chunking rule for Australian landline telephone numbers in national format.

rules.quote: Write mobile telephone numbers in 1 chunk of 4 digits and then 2 chunks of 3 digits.
rules.violation_condition: an Australian mobile phone number in national format not formatted as 4 digits followed by two chunks of 3 digits (e.g. 0491 570 159)
when: Content is intended for use within Australia.
rules.why: G-2: specific chunking specification for mobile numbers.

covers.quote: Use international format for content that will be used outside Australia.
The international format uses a plus symbol ’+’ to represent the international prefix, followed by a country code (‘61’ for Australia).

examples.note: Australian landline number in international format

rules.quote:
For landline numbers:
[aaf2f31d4fc5] LI  start with a plus symbol ‘+’ and add the country code (‘61’ for Australia)
[ab9c3e20011c] LI  add the area code without the ‘0’
[6b7b2b6e48f8] LI  write the telephone number in 2 chunks of 4 digits.
rules.violation_condition: an Australian landline telephone number intended for international audiences that does not follow the format +61 [area code without leading 0] [4 digits] [4 digits]
when: Content will be used outside Australia.
rules.why: G-2: specification for formatting Australian landlines in international format.

examples.note: Australian mobile number in international format

rules.quote:
For mobile numbers:
[b387f57ef65e] LI  start with a plus symbol ‘+’ and add the country code (‘61’ for Australia)
[fbefa13ab9b7] LI  omit the first ‘0’
[3ab957d5f8c7] LI  write the telephone number in 3 chunks of 3 digits.
rules.violation_condition: an Australian mobile phone number in international format that does not follow '+61' followed by 3 chunks of 3 digits without the leading 0
when: Content will be used outside Australia.
rules.why: G-2: specification for formatting Australian mobile numbers in international format.

rules.quote: Always write foreign telephone numbers in the international format.
rules.violation_condition: a foreign telephone number written without the international format (plus symbol prefix and country code)
rules.why: Clear distinct rule for foreign telephone numbers.

covers.quote: This is not always the case, so use HTML code to support this functionality.

examples.note: Tel link with spaces stripped in href

rules.quote: Use ‘tel:[telephone number]’ as the URL. Remove spaces between the numbers.
rules.violation_condition: a telephone number link href that does not use the 'tel:' scheme or that contains spaces within the dialling digits
when: In HTML content providing click-to-call functionality.
rules.why: G-2: specific rule for formatting click-to-call telephone URLs in HTML.

covers.quote: Don’t do this, because some people find it hard to convert letters to numbers.

rules.quote: Always display the telephone number as digits. Don’t use ‘phone words’. Use the relevant 13 or 1300 number instead.
rules.violation_condition: a telephone number written using letters/phone words (e.g. '13 VETS') instead of numeric digits
